newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Commission postpones action on tobacco subsidies.
newsitem.headline: Commission postpones action on tobacco subsidies.

text.p: The European Commission on Wednesday postponed for two weeks a decision on how to reform the EU's tobacco subsidy programme so it could study the potential effects on farmers, a Commission spokesman said.
"Obviously it will have a socio-economic impact on producers and on regions, there's no doubt about that," spokesman Joao Vale de Almeida told a news briefing.
"So the commissioners felt they should delve a little bit deeper into this point, and they'd like to give themselves another fortnight to come up with the best possible solution."

The Commission was considering a proposal by Agriculture Commissioner Franz Fischler to target production subsidies to higher-quality tobacco, offer buyouts to tobacco farmers and double the one percent levy on tobacco subsidies that is used to finance EU anti-smoking programmes.
However, Social Affairs Commissioner Padraig Flynn argued that the subsidies should be phased out completely on the grounds that they compromised the EU's effort to combat smoking-related deaths.
Eight EU countries produce tobacco, led by Italy and Germany.
